title: Recovery from a Liable Third Party, Travel Protection Plans
content:
Where a third party was liable for a loss settled under the Travel Protection Plans, the insurer may recover
what it paid, and the amount recovered restores the benefit it was taken from.

## The terms of a recovery

1. A recovery is applied against the payment it reverses and never against a different claim or a different
   policy.
2. The traveller keeps whatever the recovery exceeds, because the insurer recovers only what it actually paid.
3. A recovery never reopens a decided claim: the decision stands and only the benefit consumed is restored.
4. A plan on which recovery from a liable third party does not apply makes no recovery at all, and the
   settlement stands as paid.

## Where the traveller has already been compensated

A traveller who has been compensated for the same loss by the airline, the property or another supplier must say
so, and the settlement is reduced by what they received rather than recovered afterwards.

## Points of judgement

Where the insurer paid 1200 on a loss and afterwards recovers 1500 from the party liable for it, the traveller
keeps the 300 by which the recovery exceeds what was paid, and 1200 of benefit is restored on the policy the
payment was made under — not on a second certificate the traveller happens to hold, and not against a different
claim on the same one. The decision that allowed the claim is untouched by the recovery. The figures here are an
illustration.
